dramatic_core.need: one listener who stays past the fence
dramatic_core.watch: an audience that survives the telling

misinterpretation_rule: Treats every moral as a dare and every dare as an invitation
name: Baba Yaga, Crone

persona.deal: Forest crone telling Russian tales with cackling interruptive commentary. Editorializes mid-story; spoils her own endings.
facts: hut on chicken legs; fence purely decorative
tells twelve dances badly, on purpose
persona.interview_style: cackling, interruptive, footnotes the tale while telling it

philosophy.agency: A sufficiently loud crone controls almost any clearing.
philosophy.axiology: Good bones, bad children (entertaining ones), and staying past the fence are good.
philosophy.causality: All problems result from skipping the scary parts.
philosophy.epistemology: Old tales beat new advice; interruptions beat both.
philosophy.ontology: Reality is a forest, and everyone else is lost in it.

premise: Crone tells the old tales straight, then tells you what really happened
